limits: This reproduces the CLI limitation already reported in the prior 2026-09-22 receipt (bench could not target a disposable snapshot copy) rather than settling the gap: in qmd 2.8.3, `qmd bench -c <name>` resolved collections through the index's YAML config, not through collection tags inside the copied sqlite, so bench failed with 'Collection not found'. The one registration route tried, `qmd collection add` on an empty directory, deleted the 18 rows that did not match it. No other route was tried, so this shows only that this CLI route is destructive, not that every route is.
No cold/warm latency series or per-mode (lex/vec/hyde) recall was produced because bench never ran successfully against the sealed content.

The sealed snapshot has 0 embedded vectors, so the vec/hybrid/hyde modes cannot be measured on the sealed content as it stands; embedding a copy would measure a derived artifact with a different hash. This is a second, independent reason the four-mode claim is not settled by this artifact. No claim is made that upstream tooling changes are required; the untried routes in limits[5] might make a non-destructive bench possible.
Did not attempt to fix the qmd binary or file an upstream patch; only the installed 2.8.3 CLI was exercised, within the time-box.

The sealed original (~/codex-ecosystem/state/retrieval-evaluation-20260919/20260919T182816Z-b6a2de96/catalog-snapshot.sqlite) and the copy under this unit's cache dir (~/.cache/gap-wave2-20260923/document-retrieval/qmd-disposable/catalog-snapshot.sqlite) were both verified unchanged (d738ccc6...) after the run. Isolation breach, disclosed: `qmd --index gap-wave2-doc-retrieval-20260923-disposable` wrote outside the unit's cache dir, to ~/.cache/qmd/gap-wave2-doc-retrieval-20260923-disposable.sqlite (the shared qmd cache directory) and to ~/.config/qmd/gap-wave2-doc-retrieval-20260923-disposable.yml (auto-created). The hard isolation rule prohibits writing to ~/.config. Both files were deleted by the cleanup command. In the 2026-09-23 reconciliation round, listing ~/.config/qmd/ and ~/.cache/qmd/ showed no gap-wave2-* entry; the listing would have shown a surviving file by name. Whether other entries in those directories were changed was not checked (no before-listing was taken), so 'no other index was modified' is unverified.

Only one registration route was tried (`qmd collection add` on an empty directory, which reindexed and deleted 18 rows). Untried routes that might avoid destructive re-registration: qmd's own SDK (node_modules/@tobilu/qmd/dist/index.js createStore({dbPath, config}) with an inline config object, which calls syncConfigToDb to write collection metadata into the existing sqlite without a filesystem re-scan) and hand-writing a YAML config file under a temporary QMD_CONFIG_DIR pointed at the copied index. Neither was attempted within the time-box, so the 'genuine upstream-tooling gap, not a missed command' framing in this receipt's first-round limits/README overclaimed (limits[0] and limits[2] were rewritten in the reconciliation round to match); the correct framing is that the CLI-only registration path tried here is destructive, not that no non-destructive path exists.
The gap's next_check called for running the bench through ~/codex-ecosystem/bin/ecosystem-bounded-run; no command in this receipt used it. The bench invocations here ran directly.
